title: Light Before Einstein
tagline: He builds the mathematics of relativity — and gives Einstein the tools to prove it.

scenes.text: Leiden, Netherlands, 1895. The most fundamental mystery in physics has just deepened. The Michelson-Morley experiment has proven light travels at the same speed regardless of direction — even as Earth moves through space. This should be impossible. Hendrik Lorentz is about to try to save the old theory — and accidentally lay the foundation for the new one.

scenes.speaker: Hendrik Lorentz
scenes.text: If Maxwell's equations describe light correctly — and they do — then moving objects must contract in the direction of motion. Time itself must stretch. These are not metaphors. They are mathematical necessities.

challenge.statement: Lorentz predicted time dilation — that time moves slower for moving objects — before Einstein published his theory of relativity.
challenge.fact: Hendrik Lorentz derived the 'Lorentz transformation' equations in 1895–1904, which showed that time, length, and mass change with velocity. Einstein took these equations and provided the physical interpretation: special relativity (1905).

scenes.text: Lorentz derived the equations — now called the Lorentz transformations — describing how time and space change for objects moving near light speed. He won the Nobel Prize in 1902. Eleven years later, a young patent clerk named Einstein used those same equations — but gave them a wholly different meaning.

scenes.speaker: Hendrik Lorentz
scenes.text: Einstein says there is no ether. No absolute space. The transformations I derived as corrections to the old theory — he derives from first principles as the very nature of reality. He has seen further than I could. And he is right.

challenge.instruction: Lorentz's equations describe how a moving cylinder appears to shrink. Calculate the volume of this relativistic cylinder.
challenge.fact: Lorentz contraction predicts that a moving object appears shorter in the direction of motion. A cylinder moving at 87% of light speed would appear halved in length — its volume halved — to a stationary observer.

challenge.instruction: Lorentz's transformation equations describe a universe where time, space, and mass change with velocity — yet follow exact constraints. Fill the grid so each row, column, and 2×2 box contains 1–4 exactly once.
challenge.fact: Hendrik Lorentz derived his transformation equations in 1895–1904, showing mathematically that length, time, and mass change with velocity. Einstein took these equations and provided the physical interpretation: special relativity. Lorentz considered Einstein's insight the greater achievement.

challenge.instruction: Control the magnetic field strength to guide the charged particle to the target.
challenge.fact: The Lorentz force (F = qv × B) causes charged particles to curve in a magnetic field — the foundation of cathode ray tubes, particle accelerators, and mass spectrometers.

challenge.instruction: Léon Foucault measured the speed of light by bouncing a beam off a spinning mirror. You have one mirror — route the beam through four fixed reflectors to reach the exit.
challenge.fact: Foucault measured the speed of light at 298,000 km/s in 1850 — within 0.6% of the true value — using a rotating mirror that shifted while light was in transit. Lorentz's equations later explained why light's speed is constant for all observers.
